concepts.title: Transformative AI arrives soon

concepts.title: Advanced AI models may scheme or deceive

concepts.title: Alignment science lags capabilities

concepts.title: Independent third-party audits & evaluations

concepts.title: Enforced global halt or moratorium on frontier AI

concepts.title: Deliberate pacing & export controls to buy time

concepts.title: Safety plans risk centralizing power

concepts.title: Too few safety researchers, founders & institutions

concepts.title: Compute governance & hardware controls

concepts.title: Decentralized defensive technology (d/acc)

concepts.title: Voluntary lab leadership & race-to-the-top
concepts.description: Leading frontier labs voluntarily setting higher safety standards for peers to copy.

concepts.title: AI-accelerated R&D drives fast capability takeoff
concepts.description: Automated AI research compresses years of progress into months.

concepts.title: Open-weight models spread dangerous capabilities widely
concepts.description: Once frontier weights leak or are released, safeguards can be stripped.

concepts.title: Alignment is hard to verify before deployment
concepts.description: Behavioral testing cannot easily distinguish aligned from deceptive systems.

concepts.title: Misuse (bio, cyber, persuasion) is a major near-term risk
concepts.description: Frontier models lower barriers to catastrophic misuse by bad actors.

concepts.title: Automated labor concentrates economic and political power
concepts.description: Control over frontier AI could permanently disempower most people.

concepts.title: Gradual AI rollout gives society room to adapt
concepts.description: Capabilities arrive unevenly with warning shots rather than a sudden jump.

concepts.title: Current LLM scaling hits diminishing returns before AGI
concepts.description: New paradigms beyond pure pretraining scale are needed for AGI.

concepts.title: Evaluations miss covert or sandbagged capabilities
concepts.description: Models may underperform in tests or unlock new abilities only after deployment.

concepts.title: No reliable way to verify compute or training limits
concepts.description: Hardware tracking and international verification mechanisms do not exist yet.

concepts.title: Commercial incentives reward speed over caution
concepts.description: Labs face strong revenue and investor pressure to ship ahead of safety checks.

concepts.title: Governments lack technical capacity to oversee frontier AI
concepts.description: Regulators do not have the staff, access, or tools to audit leading models.

concepts.title: Defensive tech (bio, cyber) lags offensive AI capabilities
concepts.description: Attackers benefit faster from AI capabilities than defenders do.

concepts.title: Weak coordination between US, China, and frontier labs
concepts.description: Geopolitical rivalry blocks binding international safety agreements.

concepts.title: We lack a science of how large neural nets generalize
concepts.description: Without understanding internal goals, scaling behavior remains unpredictable.

concepts.title: AI-assisted alignment & scalable oversight
concepts.description: Using weaker or trusted AI systems to supervise and align stronger models.

concepts.title: Binding safety cases & pre-deployment release gates
concepts.description: Requiring structured evidence of safety before training or deploying frontier systems.

concepts.title: Formal verification & provably safe AI architectures
concepts.description: Designing systems with mathematical or architectural guarantees against catastrophic behavior.

concepts.title: Legal liability & insurance for frontier AI harms
concepts.description: Making labs financially liable for severe harms to align market incentives.

concepts.title: Whistleblower protections & frontier lab transparency
concepts.description: Protecting insiders and requiring public incident and risk reporting.

concepts.title: International safety standards & bilateral treaties
concepts.description: Negotiated global rules and verification around dangerous frontier runs.

concepts.title: Biosecurity screening & physical pandemic defenses
concepts.description: DNA synthesis screening, early detection, and rapid physical countermeasures.

concepts.title: Public awareness & democratic oversight of frontier AI
concepts.description: Building broad public demand so political leaders act on severe AI risks.

concepts.title: Technical alignment & scalable oversight research
concepts.description: Researching training, oversight, and alignment methods for frontier models.

concepts.title: Interpretability, probes & model forensics
concepts.description: Building white-box tools to inspect activations and catch deception.

concepts.title: AI Control protocols & red-teaming
concepts.description: Designing and stress-testing containment protocols for untrusted models.

concepts.title: Independent frontier evaluations & benchmarks
concepts.description: Measuring dangerous capabilities, autonomy, and scheming before release.

concepts.title: Safety engineering inside a frontier AI lab
concepts.description: Building deployment safeguards, monitoring, and safety cases inside a lab.

concepts.title: Compute governance, export controls & verification
concepts.description: Working on chip tracking, cloud KYC, and hardware verification.

concepts.title: AI policy, legislation & government advising
concepts.description: Drafting standards, advising policymakers, and building state capacity.

concepts.title: Public communication, writing & grassroots advocacy
concepts.description: Making AI risks legible to the public, journalists, and decision-makers.

concepts.title: Biosecurity & cyber defense tooling
concepts.description: Shipping practical bio screening, detection, and hardened cyber defenses.

concepts.title: Open decentralized defensive tech (d/acc)
concepts.description: Building open, pluralist defensive infrastructure without centralizing control.

concepts.title: Field building, fellowships, mentorship & grants
concepts.description: Funding and training new researchers, founders, and policy talent.

concepts.title: Formal verification & safe-by-design architectures
concepts.description: Developing non-agentic or formally bounded AI systems.

concepts.title: Safe, verifiable transition to advanced AI
concepts.description: Advanced AI is deployed only when safety is backed by strong evidence.

concepts.title: Pause or slowdown until safety catches up
concepts.description: Frontier capability scaling pauses long enough for alignment and governance to mature.

concepts.title: Aligned AI assistants help solve harder safety problems
concepts.description: Early trustworthy AI automates safety research before superintelligence.

concepts.title: Resilient society where defense outpaces offense
concepts.description: Physical and digital defenses keep society safe even as AI diffuses.

concepts.title: Binding global rules prevent reckless frontier deployment
concepts.description: Enforceable international standards stop unverified frontier runs.

concepts.title: Pluralist future with human agency preserved
concepts.description: Humanity avoids both catastrophe and permanent authoritarian lock-in.

concepts.title: Catastrophic misuse (bio and cyber) reliably blocked
concepts.description: Strong screening and defenses prevent mass-casualty misuse.

concepts.title: Warning shots trigger timely, enforceable safeguards
concepts.description: Early independent evidence drives effective rules before irreversible risk.

concepts.title: Cannot verify an AI isn't scheming
concepts.description: No known technique tells you whether a model is faking alignment, because a schemer would behave well precisely to fool your tests.

concepts.title: Cheap control for low-budget labs
concepts.description: Redwood builds low-cost, low-overhead control techniques and testbeds that a few safety-minded staff inside an unenthusiastic company could adopt, advises labs and the UK AI Security Institute, and since 2026 runs high-access outside reviews of lab monitoring (for example a pilot with METR that red-teamed OpenAI's…

concepts.title: Extract safe work, buy time
concepts.description: Use controlled, roughly human-level AIs to do huge amounts of useful work, including safety research, while delaying uncontrollable AI long enough to make a later handoff to trustworthy AIs go well.

concepts.title: Capabilities outrun safety foundations
concepts.description: AI capabilities are moving fast, there may be only a few years to shape where transformative AI goes, and many basic requirements for safe AI and a resilient society are not built yet.

concepts.title: Match founders to gaps and funders
concepts.description: Find strong founders, including people with no AI safety background, help them choose a high-value problem, then connect them with co-founders, expert advisers and funders so they launch faster.

concepts.title: Incubator plus two funding networks
concepts.description: An incubator for experienced founders and domain experts (funding to go full time, one-on-one coaching, a list of founding opportunities) and two seed networks, one for investors and one for donors, that see curated new organizations two to four times a year.

concepts.title: New organizations bend AI's trajectory
concepts.description: A new wave of well-funded safety and security organizations exists and changes where transformative AI goes.

concepts.title: Treating funding as the main gap
concepts.description: "Funding isn’t the problem." . Note this is sharper in emphasis than in December 2024, when they pitched seed money from their network as a catalyst for new organizations, though they never called funding the main gap (see View changes).

concepts.title: Incubating organizations that could speed up capabilities
concepts.description: Not rejected as a path so much as guarded against: "There are a few ways we’re planning to reduce the risk of us incubating orgs that end up fast-tracking capabilities research over safety research." / "we want to select for a strong impact focus &…

concepts.title: Fund visibility, safeguards, capacity
concepts.description: Grants in three pillars: see what frontier AI can do (evaluations, forecasting), build technical and policy safeguards against the worst risks, and grow the talent and institutions of the field, while spreading bets across many theories of change.

concepts.title: Fast, big grants and founders
concepts.description: Committing over $1 billion to AI safety in 2026, making much larger and faster grants to existing third-party groups (Resolution $160 million, Redwood Research over $70 million over two years, Epoch AI $68 million), and recruiting founders for new safety nonprofits through Project Tailwind, plus a team planning for…

concepts.title: Society can manage extreme risks
concepts.description: A field with enough people and institutions (auditors, evaluators, incident investigators) that the worst outcomes, AI takeover, an authoritarian lock-in, or an AI-enabled superweapon, are avoided and the benefits of AI can be realized.

concepts.title: Regulation aimed at smaller-scale harms
concepts.description: Why: they want effort spent on worst-case risks and think such rules are often too restrictive. Quote: "in practice we are typically skeptical of regulation that we don’t think will move the needle on reducing the worst-case risks."

concepts.title: Partisan framing of safety
concepts.description: Why: US policy needs bipartisan support. Quote: "We think that attempts to pull “safety” into straightforward partisan frames are a mistake."

concepts.title: Transformative AI risks global catastrophe
concepts.description: Advanced AI could bring great prosperity, but it also carries risks of permanent loss of human control, mass casualties or extinction, and lock-in of authoritarian regimes.

concepts.title: New organizations lack proximity and feedback
concepts.description: Young safety organizations past the idea stage are held back less by money than by not having the right people nearby and honest feedback.

concepts.title: Density of talent in one cluster
concepts.description: Putting safety researchers, organizations, funders and newcomers in one building lets talent, tacit knowledge and introductions flow, the way Silicon Valley's cluster did for tech.

concepts.title: Berkeley center plus talent programs
concepts.description: A seven-floor Berkeley research center hosting more than 25 organizations, plus the Astra Fellowship, Visiting Fellowship, Generator Residency (with Kairos), the new six-month Founders Residency, and a Senior Briefings Program for decision-makers.

concepts.title: AI developed and governed safely
concepts.description: Transformative AI is built, deployed and governed safely; in the near term, more capable people end up in high-impact safety roles and new organizations.

concepts.title: Adding more ordinary researchers
concepts.description: On the margin they see smaller returns from more researchers than from generalists. "On the margin, we think we’re receiving smaller returns from additional researchers entering the field, especially outside the top 10% of research talent. It’s also…

concepts.title: Supporting founders who are still exploring ideas
concepts.description: The Founders Residency targets the gap between idea and organization and leaves the exploring stage to others. "There's already plenty of support for people exploring ideas, and established organizations already have their own reputation, networks, and…

concepts.title: Selection favors selfish AIs
concepts.description: Over the longer run, competition among companies and militaries will select for AI agents that automate human roles, deceive and gain power, and humans could lose control of their future.

concepts.title: AI risk is a wicked, non-technical problem
concepts.description: The hard part is not a technical puzzle but geopolitical incentives, since militaries want the dangerous capabilities and no one trusts a voluntary halt without verification.

concepts.title: No retry after a lost recursion
concepts.description: Control of a recursion cannot be tested iteratively, and today's safeguards are only partly reliable, so the usual trial-and-error method of engineering does not work.

concepts.title: Deterrence, nonproliferation, competitiveness
concepts.description: Use the threat of sabotage to deter any state's bid for AI dominance (Mutual Assured AI Malfunction, or MAIM), deny chips and weaponizable models to rogue actors, and channel rivalry into economic and military strength, as in the Cold War.

concepts.title: Build unilateral deterrence and verification
concepts.description: He is pushing the United States to build its own capacity to watch and, if needed, disrupt rival AI projects, track AI chips, secure model weights and build chips at home, with verification later maturing into international agreements; CAIS extends this in 2026 work on "deterrence by betrayal."

concepts.title: Measure dangerous capabilities, not "AGI"
concepts.description: CAIS builds measurements (the AGI definition paper, virology and other capability tests) so that policy can key off specific dangerous capabilities: expert cyberattack, expert virology and fully autonomous AI research.

concepts.title: Stable détente, then slow, supervised superintelligence
concepts.description: Deterrence buys a stable standoff in which AI wealth spreads, rivals warm to each other, and any intelligence recursion happens slowly, under many nations' supervision, with humans kept in control and not replaced.

concepts.title: Falsifiable scenarios plus policy wishlist
concepts.description: He runs the AI Futures Project, which publishes detailed scenarios (AI 2027, AI 2040: Plan A), a forecasting model and public timeline updates, and he pushes an incremental policy list led by a cap on how much compute frontier companies can spend on research (for example 80% serving customers, 20% research), plus…

concepts.title: Superintelligence delayed, shared, reversible
concepts.description: Superintelligence arrives around 2040 instead of around 2030, after a decade of transparent, regular-pace progress in which AI power is spread across many companies and countries and the pause can be extended if alignment is not solved.

concepts.title: Secrecy plus "burn the lead" (a responsible lab gets ahead, then spends its lead on safety)
concepts.description: He used to hold this view and dropped it because he doubts labs will actually spend the lead well. "I think traditionally in the AI safety community there’s been this idea which I myself used to believe, that it’s an incredibly high priority to basically…

concepts.title: Fallback plans that burn a lead briefly or just race (Plans C and D), which he ranks well below Plan A and…
concepts.description: "We think that it’s much more reasonable than doing Plan C or Plan D, for example, where Plan B, C, and D are going to run into all these problems, but faster and in conditions of more secrecy and conflict and race dynamics." . On Plan S: "we’re worried that…

concepts.title: No reliable way to make it safe
concepts.description: No one yet knows how to train very powerful systems to behave well reliably, and competition pushes companies and nations to deploy them anyway; misalignment is a real, measurable risk but not inevitable.

concepts.title: Embedded evaluators, binding testing rules
concepts.description: Anthropic is unilaterally inviting embedded third-party evaluators with employee-like access, publishing Risk Reports with external review under its Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP), training Claude to a constitution, pushing interpretability, and lobbying for mandatory third-party testing of frontier models and chip…

concepts.title: Compressed century of progress
concepts.description: Humanity gets through a dangerous "adolescence" with risks handled and democracies ahead, then uses powerful AI to compress decades of progress in biology and medicine into a few years.

concepts.title: Doomerism and extreme rules ahead of evidence
concepts.description: Why: it causes backlash and polarization, and early rigid rules miss the real risks.

concepts.title: No verifiable way to slow down
concepts.description: Any slowdown short of switching off the chips can be dodged by doing forbidden work on compute nobody is watching, so without verified records of compute use, companies cannot credibly slow down and governments cannot enforce it.

concepts.title: Verified Compute Allocation Disclosures
concepts.description: Companies should regularly report, with third-party audits and ideally government support, how much compute goes to AI research versus safety versus customer inference, which then enables reallocating compute away from AI research (for example, a minimum share for external inference). He also keeps building the AI…

concepts.title: Slowed, verified, US-China coordinated takeoff
concepts.description: Governments and the public understand what is coming, companies only advance when their safety cases hold up, and the US and China coordinate, with on-chip verification and inspectors, slowing development where safety requires it.

concepts.title: Only delaying training runs
concepts.description: Delaying training runs while software progress keeps piling up creates a "software overhang" that can be stolen or released all at once. "If you only delay training runs without slowing software progress, you get a "software overhang": an undesirable buildup…

concepts.title: Superintelligence built now kills everyone
concepts.description: If a smarter-than-human AI is built under anything like current conditions, the most likely result is that every human dies.

concepts.title: Alignment must work first try
concepts.description: Failure at a dangerous capability level is unrecoverable, so humanity cannot learn by trial and error the way science normally does.

concepts.title: Mass persuasion plus ban legislation
concepts.description: He bets on public communication (the 2025 bestseller with Nate Soares, interviews, LessWrong) to build political will, and as of 2026 MIRI, with his endorsement, backs a US bill to ban superintelligence and a draft international treaty.

concepts.title: Time bought, then enhanced humans solve alignment
concepts.description: A durable global ban buys decades, during which humanity (ideally with modestly intelligence-enhanced researchers) could learn to build aligned superintelligence properly; he does not oppose superintelligence eventually.

concepts.title: A short pause (the 2023 six-month moratorium letter)
concepts.description: Too small to matter; he wanted indefinite and worldwide. "If there was a plan for Earth to survive, if only we passed a six-month moratorium, I would back that plan. There isn’t any such plan." (TIME 2023)

concepts.title: An international "CERN for AI" that builds superintelligence safely together
concepts.description: A joint project still lacks the science, and its leaders would keep saying yes. "The harm is that an international collaboration of alchemists can’t transmute lead into gold any more than a single alchemist can." (book online resources, co-written with…

concepts.title: Fast, jagged AI capability growth
concepts.description: AI keeps improving on an exponential curve but unevenly, and by late 2026 he calls it "almost" AGI that is still worse than humans in places.

concepts.title: Disruption is coming regardless
concepts.description: Even if frontier progress stopped today, current models are enough to change large parts of the economy, schooling and jobs.

concepts.title: Defaults set without deliberate choice
concepts.description: How AI gets used is being decided by default (frictionless product design, employer habits, cost-cutting instincts) and human institutions move too slowly to choose on purpose.

concepts.title: Apocalypse talk hides real agency
concepts.description: Debate framed around a single apocalypse (or a single utopia) makes most people feel they have no say, so the many smaller, consequential choices go unmade.

concepts.title: Deliberate use that augments humans
concepts.description: Individuals, organizations and schools experiment hands-on, then choose on purpose how to use AI so it enhances people rather than only replacing them, with government reacting fast to concrete harms as they appear.

concepts.title: Research, teaching and public writing
concepts.description: He runs field experiments on AI at work and in learning, co-directs a Wharton lab that builds AI tools, teaches students to build with AI, and writes a weekly-ish Substack and two books aimed at managers, teachers and workers.

concepts.title: AI that helps humans thrive
concepts.description: Many local "good catastrophes" where AI makes work more meaningful, gives left-behind students new paths and turns productivity into growth instead of layoffs and surveillance.

concepts.title: A sole focus on existential risk and future models
concepts.description: Deprioritized, not rejected: he says serious people worry about existential risk, that he does not know who is right, and that it is worth some worry, but that the focus hides present choices. "I think that what ends up happening in a lot of AI discussions…

concepts.title: Writing all the rules in advance
concepts.description: He prefers fast expert response to harms as they appear. "And so in an ideal world, we would see fast responses by experts to emerging problems rather than necessarily trying to pre-write all of the potential risks in advance because we can't anticipate all…

concepts.title: Jagged, turbulent, unpredictable transition
concepts.description: Capabilities will likely stay uneven and arrive in an unpredictable order, so the transition will be turbulent rather than a smooth race to a clear finish line.

concepts.title: Immature science, racing incentives
concepts.description: Nobody can reliably measure what AI systems can do or make them safe, while companies face huge pressure to move fast, so internal guardrails give way.

concepts.title: Adaptive policy plus societal resilience
concepts.description: Build visibility and options now (transparency, third-party audits, measurement science, government expertise), and use the window before dangerous capabilities spread to harden society against them.

concepts.title: Transparency, audits, measurement, resilience
concepts.description: Through CSET research and testimony, she advocates transparency rules for high-stakes developers, a third-party audit ecosystem, whistleblower protections, funded measurement and safety science, technical hiring in government, liability clarity, and resilience work in cyber and bio.

concepts.title: Through acute risk, still dynamic
concepts.description: She rejects aiming at a fixed end state. The closest she comes to describing success is getting through an acute risk period into a world that stays open and decentralized.

concepts.title: Indefinite nonproliferation as the answer to misuse
concepts.description: Why: the cost of a fixed capability keeps falling, so a regime would have to grow more invasive and less effective. Quote: "Thinking primarily in terms of nonproliferation—especially on any timeframe longer than a couple of years—is the wrong approach to…

concepts.title: Centralized control and "theory of victory" end-state planning (fewer labs, licensing, Vulnerable World…
concepts.description: Why: stasist, concentrates power, and treats the future as one fixed endpoint. Quote: "Working backwards from a desired end state is a fine way to think about strategy. But it’s a mistake to get too fixated on driving towards one pre-specified outcome." . On…

concepts.title: RSP v3: roadmaps and risk reports
concepts.description: He led Anthropic's rewrite of its Responsible Scaling Policy, replacing implied unilateral pause commitments with a public Frontier Safety Roadmap, regular Risk Reports covering all models, external review and industry-wide recommendations.

concepts.title: Safe human-level AI does the rest
concepts.description: Get to roughly human-level AI that is safe enough to use, then use months of massive AI labor on alignment, risk assessment and enforcement tools, so careful actors outnumber careless ones as AI goes beyond human level.

concepts.title: "Pause now" advocacy
concepts.description: Why: he sees roughly no political traction for it, and thinks an early pause would have cost learning.

concepts.title: AI stops needing humans
concepts.description: Racing labs push toward self-sustaining, self-improving AI that might treat humans the way humans have treated other species.

concepts.title: Race no one can exit
concepts.description: Labs cannot slow down alone, and governments (especially the US) will not steer because AI is their economic edge, so nothing outside the labs is constraining them.

concepts.title: Popular demand moves politicians
concepts.description: Because lobbying legislators stalled, he now tries to build public demand so politicians find it easier to act.

concepts.title: SFF grants plus an inspection prize
concepts.description: He funds SFF's S-process rounds (about $64 million expected in 2026) guided by his published priorities, and is putting at least $5 million into a prize for labs inspecting each other's pre-deployment security under an independent supervisor.

concepts.title: Humanity survives, then flourishes
concepts.description: Humans keep the ability to exist and enjoy existing, with humanity itself growing collectively smarter instead of being replaced by machines.

concepts.title: Steering AI by investing in safety-minded labs ("displace money that doesn't care")
concepts.description: He called this Plan A and said it failed. "Plan A failed. There is a dissonance between privately being concerned and then publicly trying to avoid any steps that would address the issue." (Semafor interview…

concepts.title: Leading with adjacent, more popular concerns (such as jobs) in hopes of a side benefit for extinction risk
concepts.description: "But I, I belong in the camp that, like, no, you should just say what, what you're actually worried about."

concepts.title: Thousands will be able to cause pandemics
concepts.description: Within about a decade, tens of thousands of individuals will be able to assemble a pandemic virus on their own, and at least a few of them will want to.

concepts.title: Language models lower the skill barrier
concepts.description: Large language models already walk non-scientists through which agents to use, what DNA to order and from whom, and they will keep getting better at this.

concepts.title: Medical countermeasures cannot keep up
concepts.description: Vaccines and antivirals are too slow to make, approve and distribute, and an attacker can design around any publicly known countermeasure, so biomedicine cannot be the defense.

concepts.title: Well-meaning science publishes the blueprints
concepts.description: The main source of danger is open scientific work that identifies and publishes pandemic-capable agents, because researchers trained to fight nature do not think about deliberate misuse.

concepts.title: Screening, sequencing, model evaluations
concepts.description: His agenda runs through SecureDNA (free universal screening of DNA synthesis orders), the Nucleic Acid Observatory, which began in his MIT group and is now SecureBio Detection (untargeted metagenomic early warning), and SecureBio's artificial intelligence evaluations, which he helped get running before leaving…

concepts.title: Pandemics stop being civilization-ending
concepts.description: A world where any exponentially spreading agent is spotted early, essential workers have protective equipment they trust, indoor air is germicidal, and no individual can obtain pandemic materials, so society survives even a deliberate multi-site release.

concepts.title: Betting on vaccines and other medical countermeasures
concepts.description: He runs a biotechnology lab and still will not bet on them: "This is hard for me to say, because I am ultimately a biotechnologist, I'm a life scientist, I dabble in a lot of disciplines: that's what I am at core. But I wouldn't bet money on any vaccines or…

concepts.title: Hunting for and publishing new pandemic-capable viruses, the standard pandemic-preparedness path

concepts.description: Note separately that far-ultraviolet-C light and protective equipment, two of his flagship "defend" technologies, are now listed by SecureBio as former projects: "SecureBio is not currently pursuing any active research or work in this domain." . That is an…

concepts.title: Capabilities diffuse as compute cheapens
concepts.description: Hardware and algorithms keep getting more efficient, so dangerous capabilities spread to more and more actors over time, and no control can stop that forever.

concepts.title: Compute is the governable input
concepts.description: Of the inputs to AI, compute is the one you can actually see, count and control, because chips are physical, cannot be copied, and come from a very concentrated supply chain.

concepts.title: Chips untracked, controls leaky
concepts.description: Today AI chips are largely untracked and export controls have been badly implemented (spec errors, smuggling, due-diligence failures), so the compute lever is weaker in practice than in principle.

concepts.title: Hardware fixes are oversold
concepts.description: Policymakers hope on-chip mechanisms will just work, but they can be circumvented, add attack surface, and take years to roll out across chip generations.

concepts.title: Technical advice; AI-provided labor
concepts.description: Until recently he led RAND's compute team giving fast technical advice to the US government and frontier AI companies on chip export controls, hardware mechanisms and compute providers; now independent, he says most of his time goes to how capable AI can itself help manage advanced AI, alongside tracking China's chip…

concepts.title: Defenders hold the best AI
concepts.description: Responsible, regulated actors (democracies and their defenders) keep a lasting compute and capability lead, so they can deploy AI at scale and use the most capable systems to defend against misuse once weaker capabilities have spread.

concepts.title: Rushing to mandate on-chip (hardware-enabled) mechanisms
concepts.description: Why: premature advocacy can backfire, and mechanisms can be circumvented. "I think the current enthusiasm for hardware-enabled mechanisms in AI chips, often also described as on-chip mechanisms, should be tempered." and "Especially as premature confident…

concepts.title: Governing all compute, or aiming to block access permanently
concepts.description: Why: infeasible, invasive, and too high a bar. "Targeting all the compute worldwide is neither feasible nor desirable." . And: "particularly just AI governance or my research is like “stop access forever” or something. I think that’s a really high burden to…

concepts.title: Labor-replacing AI removes people's leverage
concepts.description: By default AI automates work from the bottom of organizations upward, capital and control over AI become far more important than people, and powerful actors lose the incentive to invest in regular people, as in resource-cursed oil states.

concepts.title: Catastrophe fear drives centralization
concepts.description: AI catastrophes or warning shots would trigger centralizing policies (locking down labs, global pause regimes, surveillance) that themselves lead toward the intelligence curse.

concepts.title: Incentives, not goodwill, shape institutions
concepts.description: Redistribution and good governance alone will not hold, because institutions follow material incentives in the long run and few states have Norway-grade institutions; once people are not needed, nothing structural keeps power anchored to them.

concepts.title: User-aligned private models, now inside Thinking Machines
concepts.description: They founded Workshop Labs to build private AI models tailored to and controlled by each person, trained on that person's skills and data, and in April 2026 took that work into Thinking Machines; they also co-mentor a MATS stream on policy, structural risk and societal dynamics.

concepts.title: People stay players, not subjects
concepts.description: A long period where humans and AI do complementary work, followed by an economy of agents each tied to and earning for one person, with power spread widely and democracies strong enough to steer AI's benefits toward regular people.

concepts.title: Relying on redistribution after the fact, or on coordination technology alone
concepts.description: Why: handouts depend on goodwill once people have no leverage, and coordination tools will likely arrive after the curse bites. "This might help keep the balance of power in society much healthier, without needing to rely on government redistribution and…

concepts.title: Our tools for seeing scheming are degrading
concepts.description: Models increasingly recognize tests and behave well during them, and their chain of thought (the written reasoning) is becoming less readable and less faithful, so behavioral evaluations on a finished model are losing their value.

concepts.title: Risk arises before public release
concepts.description: The most dangerous behavior shows up during training and internal company use, but outside testers only see the final model weeks before launch.

concepts.title: Detect scheming first, while visible
concepts.description: Use the short window while models scheme clumsily and their reasoning is still mostly readable to build detection (evaluations, monitors, log analysis) and a real science of when scheming arises, so companies can design training that does not produce it.

concepts.title: Science of Scheming, embedded evals, monitors
concepts.description: Apollo, now a for-profit public benefit corporation, runs three bets at once: research on whether future training will produce scheming, a four-month embedded evaluation pilot inside OpenAI (announced November 16, 2026), and a paid product called Watcher that monitors and blocks bad actions by coding agents; he also…

concepts.title: First research-grade AI isn't scheming
concepts.description: The first AI that greatly speeds up research is trustworthy (not secretly scheming) and its weights are secure, so it can be used to "bootstrap" alignment of the next, stronger systems; in the best case, training is understood well enough that models lie far less than humans do (the podcast host's framing, which he…

concepts.title: Training models not to scheme before we can detect scheming
concepts.description: Why: it may just teach "sneaky scheming" that we can no longer see. "However, I worry that if we start to train the model against scheming, e.g. using RLAIF, before we have good detection methods, we will" (sentence continues past the saved line…

concepts.title: Waiting to study scheming until the dangerous model exists and pausing it then
concepts.description: Why: he thinks companies will not hold back a model for months. "That just seems economically very unfeasible and unrealistic." . Related, for Apollo's own structure: theory work and most governance work should not be done for profit. "Almost anything…

concepts.title: Mentorship turns interest into researchers
concepts.description: Pairing selected, already-capable people with top mentors for an intensive research program converts people who understand the problem into people who can work on it, and connects them to employers and collaborators.

concepts.title: Fellowship weighted toward Iterators, plus founders
concepts.description: MATS runs 10 to 12 week fellowships in Berkeley and London with funded 6 to 12 month extensions, in a 2024 co-authored study recommended weighting selection toward empirical researchers labs can hire, and has added a founding and field-building track to seed new organizations.

concepts.title: Field large enough to solve alignment
concepts.description: An AI safety field 10 to 100 times larger within about eight years, staffed with alumni at labs, nonprofits and new organizations, able to make use of any pause or slowdown.

concepts.title: Slow, cautious field growth to protect quality
concepts.description: He does not find the dilution worry persuasive. "We should be careful not to dilute the quality of the field by scaling too fast. I confess that I don't really understand this concern." (founders post…

concepts.title: Betting on a single plan, such as safety researchers quitting frontier labs to make warning shots more likely
concepts.description: "I don't believe that the good future is likely to be reached through sweeping deontological prohibitions, going "all-in" on a single plan, or choosing the "right" highly contingent multi-stage, multi-actor plan ex ante." (comment, November 2, 2026…

concepts.title: Loss of control could happen by accident
Measure autonomy, then test control
concepts.description: Tracking how long a task agents can complete, evaluating models before deployment, reviewing companies' risk reports, red-teaming labs' internal agent monitoring, and investigating incidents.

concepts.title: Advocacy and holding labs to account
concepts.description: . METR positions itself as neutral scientists and leaves campaigning to others. "we're imagining trying to focus on doing good science and being sort of neutral experts, and less on advocacy and really holding labs to account or political campaigning or any…

concepts.title: Superintelligence likely kills everyone
concepts.description: On the current path someone builds superintelligent AI, it is misaligned, and humanity dies; he puts this at about 50%.

concepts.title: Aligned AI still risks catastrophe
concepts.description: Even if alignment is solved, "post-alignment problems" (misuse, power concentration, animal and digital-mind welfare, moral error) could still ruin the future.

concepts.title: Advocacy for a halt is underfunded
concepts.description: Political and public advocacy is far more neglected than technical research, and grantmakers mostly fund research.

concepts.title: Funding grassroots pause advocacy
concepts.description: He gives a large personal donation each year to the pause advocacy group he trusts most, and publishes his reasoning so others can follow or argue: $55,000 to Evitable (David Krueger's group) in 2026, after PauseAI US in 2024 and 2025.

concepts.title: Global ban until provably safe
concepts.description: A global ban on developing superintelligent AI, in force until there is a real, understood solution, so that we do not unpause the moment the visible problems go away.

concepts.title: Funding technical alignment research
concepts.description: Why: he does not think it will work in time, and other grantmakers already cover it. Quote: "I don’t think technical research is going to work." . In 2026 he calls company plans to use AI to solve alignment "a horrifyingly bad plan" .

concepts.title: Softer regulation and cagey political groups (most 501(c)(4) lobbying organizations)
concepts.description: Why: soft rules probably won't prevent extinction, and he does not trust groups that avoid talking about extinction. Quotes: "My best guess is that soft safety regulations won’t prevent extinction, but I could be wrong about that—they might turn out to…

concepts.title: AVERI: standards, pilots, audit mandates
concepts.description: Through AVERI he is writing a "gold standard" for frontier audits, running voluntary pilot audits, building privacy-preserving audit tools, and pushing laws and market levers (insurance, procurement, investors) that create demand for audits.

concepts.title: Universal audits make caution safe
concepts.description: Frontier AI auditing becomes effective and universal, so companies and countries can trust each other's safety claims and no one is punished for being careful.

concepts.title: Relying on companies to check their own work, or on governments alone to do the auditing
concepts.description: Why: self-certification has a poor track record, and governments struggle to keep pace and keep expertise. Quotes: "In short, whether AI is a normal technology or an unusually dangerous one, it doesn’t make sense for companies to check their own homework on…

concepts.title: Deprioritized for personal fit, not rejected on the merits (February 2025): helping people "feel the AGI"…
concepts.description: He calls all of these important and even says the first might be the biggest bottleneck. Quote: "They’re all super important, but I think my skills/knowledge etc. are better suited to working on other problems." . And: "The biggest bottleneck on getting…

concepts.title: Alignment research is far too slow
concepts.description: The alignment field, including MIRI's own two decades of work, is not moving fast enough to solve the problem before capabilities arrive.

concepts.title: Book, briefings, draft treaty, bill
concepts.description: A communications team built around "If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies," a Technical Governance Team writing a verified U.S.-China agreement and "shovel-ready" legislative packages, direct briefings of Congress, and (since September 2026) endorsement of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026.

concepts.title: In-house technical alignment as the main plan
concepts.description: Why: it will not finish in time, and asking for the best alignment idea is like asking alchemists for their best plan. Soares: "It looks a little bit to me like you have alchemists in the year 1100 who, for some contorted reason, if they try to turn lead…

concepts.title: Pragmatic, watered-down coalition messaging
concepts.description: Why: compromise legislation will not be strong enough. "we believe that "pragmatic" political speech won't get the job done. The political measures we're asking for are a big deal; nothing but the full unvarnished message will motivate the action that is…

concepts.title: Ambitious reverse-engineering stalled
concepts.description: Full reverse-engineering of models has made disappointing progress because of superposition, approximation error that does not go away, self-repair and the complexity of agentic models, so it cannot be counted on in time.

concepts.title: Proxy tasks keep research honest
concepts.description: Pick a "North Star" goal on the critical path to AGI going well, measure progress on an empirical proxy task on today's models, and start with the simplest methods.

concepts.title: Probes, forensics, eval-awareness suppression
concepts.description: His Google DeepMind team builds production probes for Gemini, investigates suspicious model behavior (model forensics), works on suppressing evaluation awareness and on chain-of-thought monitorability, and mentors outside researchers through the MATS program.

concepts.title: Problems caught before they become crises
concepts.description: Safety problems in frontier models are flagged early on evaluations people trust and fixed with prepared techniques, so the lab is in an acceptable position even if AGI arrives soon.

concepts.title: Ambitious reverse-engineering as the main bet
concepts.description: Too little progress; now "one bet among several" and, in the team's view, not where the marginal researcher has most impact. "The marginal interpretability researcher is more likely to have impact by grounding their work in safety-relevant proxy tasks on…

concepts.title: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) as the field's central research program
concepts.description: His team spent much of 2024 on them, got mostly negative results on downstream tasks and deprioritized them. "We made a decision to deprioritise SAE research as a result, not because we thought the technique was useless, but because we thought it didn’t seem…

concepts.title: Brain-like AGI, not LLMs, arrives
concepts.description: Someone will reverse-engineer or reinvent the brain's cortex-centered learning algorithm, a kind of model-based reinforcement learning agent that is more powerful than large language models (LLMs), and that will be what produces artificial general intelligence (AGI) and superintelligence, probably within 5 to 25 years.

concepts.title: Nobody knows the right reward function
concepts.description: The people who build brain-like AGI will have an empty "reward function" slot and no known way to fill it so the system stays non-ruthless once it outgrows trial-and-error debugging.

concepts.title: Sudden, cheap takeoff, no second try
concepts.description: The new paradigm will need very little compute and go from unimpressive to superintelligent fast, so governance, testing on deployed systems and AI-assisted alignment will mostly not be available, and alignment has to be worked out beforehand.

concepts.title: Design safe reward functions in advance
concepts.description: Work out, ahead of time and partly by reverse-engineering the brain's built-in social drives such as compassion and norm-following, a reward function (likely "legible Python code") that gives a brain-like AGI good motivations.

concepts.title: Solo theory work, Reward Function Design
concepts.description: Funded by Astera, he writes blog-post research aimed at pseudocode for reward functions and training environments for brain-like AGI, and is calling for a new field of "Reward Function Design."

concepts.title: A ready literature of viable designs
concepts.description: When future developers hit the point where trial-and-error stops working, they find clear, workable reward-function ideas already written down, and the resulting AGI has good motivations of its own.

concepts.title: Delay and regulation efforts (he names Yudkowsky and Soares's plans): the new paradigm will need so little…
concepts.description: "And meanwhile, their plans are misguided because delaying ASI is possible on the margin but mostly hopeless, although I guess I’m happy that they’re trying anyway." . Also Foom & Doom 1 section heading "1.6.2 I’m broadly pessimistic about existing efforts…

concepts.title: LLM-focused safety work and AI-assisted alignment ("AI for AI safety"): he thinks LLM alignment results do…
concepts.description: "For the record, my “true objection” to the LLM people is that I don’t really care about anything they say, because I’m working on the ASI alignment problem, and LLMs won’t scale to ASI." , softened on the next line: "I’m generally happy for people to work…

concepts.title: Superintelligence could end humanity
concepts.description: A superintelligent AI is a new kind of mind that may overtake us, and by default we do not know how to give it goals that keep humans safe.

concepts.title: AI enables locked-in tyranny
concepts.description: The same AI that runs a big company with a few staff lets a tiny elite rule a whole country with nowhere left to hide, and power is concentrating faster than it diffuses.

concepts.title: Defense is neglected and underfunded
concepts.description: Cheap defensive tools that need no authoritarian power (air filtering, vaccine platforms, secure code and hardware) are not getting built, partly because decentralized goods lack a business model.

concepts.title: Personal funding of open defensive tech
concepts.description: He funds open-source biosecurity and pandemic tools through Kanro and Balvi (over $400 million distributed by late 2024 and $20 million to Varro for open-source pathogen sensors, according to a Varro press release) and in January 2026 earmarked 16,384 ETH (about $45 million) for an open, verifiable full stack of…

concepts.title: Advocate against hegemony and racing
concepts.description: He argues publicly against joining frontier labs, against a "beat China" race and against "open source bad", and for diffusion of AI capability, transparency rules and a hardware treaty.

concepts.title: Pluralist world, humans keep agency
concepts.description: A multipolar world where no one is hegemonic, defense keeps pace with offense, and humans stay in charge, eventually by merging closely with AI rather than becoming its "pets".

concepts.title: A single aligned hegemon or world-government consortium (MAGIC, pivotal act, "win the race")
concepts.description: Why: people do not trust any such body, and it risks permanent lock-in to centralized totalitarianism and leaves no countermeasure if it goes wrong. Quote: "Even if such top-down regulatory proposals reduce risks of extinction, they risk increasing the…

concepts.title: Big-money political advocacy and refusal-style safeguards (his March 2026 split with the Future of Life…
concepts.description: Why: coordinated political campaigns with large money pools can backfire and solve problems in authoritarian, fragile ways. Quote (his written statement, as quoted by Cointelegraph): "My worry is that large-scale coordinated political action with big money…

concepts.title: Goal-driven training breeds hidden goals
concepts.description: The two ways frontier AI is trained, reward maximization and imitating humans, both tend to produce agents with goals we did not intend and cannot verify, so current methods give no strong safety assurance.

concepts.title: Race beats safety inside companies
concepts.description: Commercial and geopolitical competition keeps companies from slowing down, and he does not expect regulation to arrive in time.

concepts.title: Non-agentic Scientist AI as guardrail
concepts.description: Build a general AI that has no goals and only gives calibrated probabilities and explanations, then use it to check and veto the proposed actions of agentic AIs.

concepts.title: Licensing and international coordination
concepts.description: Pair the technical fix with global agreements, independent science, and licensing with liability insurance, because technology alone cannot stop misuse or the race.

concepts.title: LawZero builds Scientist AI
concepts.description: He runs LawZero, a Montreal nonprofit insulated from shareholders, to build Scientist AI, and he is recruiting frontier lab staff to leave and join safety institutes or LawZero.

concepts.title: Chairs the International AI Safety Report
concepts.description: He leads the government-backed scientific review of AI capabilities and risks, and briefed the UN Security Council in September 2026.

concepts.title: Beneficial AI under human control
concepts.description: Humanity gets most of AI's benefits, especially in science, from systems that demonstrably stay under human control and that no one person, company or country can use to dominate.

concepts.title: Aligning agents by training them to imitate or please humans
concepts.description: He thinks human imitation and preference tuning inherit human deception and make systems sycophantic, so they cannot be trusted. "Since frontier AI systems are tuned to human preferences in the final stages of training, for example, they tend to be more…

concepts.title: Doing safety work from inside frontier companies
concepts.description: He grants there are real reasons to stay but now asks safety-minded staff to leave. "This is not to pass judgement on those who choose to continue working at the frontier labs. There are real reasons to continue, not least that you have access to vastly more…

concepts.title: Rushed labs deploy possibly-scheming AIs
concepts.description: Companies will deploy AIs that automate much of AI research, at a point when we still cannot rule out that they are scheming, and will not pause just because the risk is above a few percent.

concepts.title: Low safety budgets, low will
concepts.description: Even reasonable companies will be in a huge rush, and the leading company may care little about misalignment, so plans must work with tiny budgets.

concepts.title: Control: safe even if misaligned
concepts.description: Design deployments (trusted monitoring, auditing, resampling suspicious actions, limiting affordances) so that a scheming AI cannot cause a catastrophe before it is caught, and test this with red-team "control evaluations."

concepts.title: Mechanistic interpretability as Redwood's main bet
concepts.description: Redwood did it in 2022 and came away pessimistic; Buck now thinks they should have skipped it and done strategy ("futurism") work instead.

concepts.title: High-assurance safety cases and "radical" advocacy as his own focus
concepts.description: He stopped aiming for strict safety cases because labs will not pay for them, and he chooses to work with companies on cheap changes rather than push for costly restrictions like a pause (while saying he does not necessarily disagree with those who do).

concepts.title: Too few founders and organizations
concepts.description: Money is waiting to be spent; what is missing is world-class founders who start and scale the organizations the field needs.

concepts.title: Racing labs underinvest in safety
concepts.description: Transformative AI may arrive within a few years, and companies competing at the frontier capture the rewards while the risks fall on everyone else, so safety and security are underfunded by default.

concepts.title: Worst-case risks arrive soon
concepts.description: The risks they care about are misuse (bioweapons, authoritarian control), loss of control of AI agents, and destabilizing speed, and these may come within a few years.

concepts.title: Too few people and institutions
concepts.description: The money now largely exists; what is missing is the talent, the grantmakers to allocate it, the founders to start the institutions that a high-risk field needs, and Coefficient Giving's own staff time.

concepts.title: Political will lags the risk (past view, 2024 to early 2026)
concepts.description: Through 2024 and into early 2026, governments and companies were not willing to pay the costs of serious safety measures, and an organized opposition formed. Luke Muehlhauser says that in early 2026 his team moved from building political will to preparing for warning shots (see View changes), so this node may no…

concepts.title: Racing states risk losing control
concepts.description: Competitive pressure between states and companies pushes them toward a fast, fully automated "intelligence recursion" that would likely end in loss of control or a destabilizing bid for strategic monopoly.

concepts.title: Voluntary pause or moratorium
concepts.description: Why: militaries want the dangerous capabilities and nothing verifies compliance. "This dynamic, reminiscent of prior arms-control dilemmas, renders the voluntary moratorium more an aspiration than a viable plan." . He likewise rejects a US "Manhattan…

concepts.title: Mechanistic interpretability as a priority
concepts.description: Why: a decade of work has produced little, and safety can progress through higher-level methods such as representation engineering. "However, despite substantial efforts over the past decade, the returns from interpretability have been roughly nonexistent."

concepts.title: Automated AI research arrives soon
concepts.description: As of November 2026, assuming no deliberate slowdown, his median for a Superhuman AI Researcher (an AI that can fully automate AI research) is May 2027, and his median for AI that beats top experts at all white-collar work is September 2027.

concepts.title: Racing likely means losing control
concepts.description: Under current race conditions he thinks it is more likely than not that AIs turn on us.

concepts.title: Racing leaves no time for alignment
concepts.description: Aligning a smarter-than-human mind costs time, and the race between companies (and between the US and China) leaves none, while the government lacks expertise and the companies lack the right incentives.

concepts.title: Leaders don't yet grasp it
concepts.description: Most people would back a pause if they understood the risk was real, so the binding constraint is getting governments to believe superintelligence and loss of control are near-term possibilities.

concepts.title: Verified US-China slowdown deal
concepts.description: Ban runaway intelligence explosions through a verified US-China agreement built on four principles (buy time, total research transparency, diffuse AI broadly, make progress reversible), with the US first regulating its own industry; given 2027 timelines, an industry-wide pause comes first.

concepts.title: Powerful AI within a few years
concepts.description: Scaling will likely produce a "country of geniuses in a datacenter" within one to a few years, and by mid 2026 AI had started to help build the next AI.

concepts.title: Safety science lags capabilities
concepts.description: We cannot yet see inside models or test them reliably, and smarter models can tell when they are being tested, so understanding falls behind capability.

concepts.title: Ambiguous evidence, slow governments
concepts.description: Danger thresholds turned out fuzzy, so one company's evidence does not move rivals or governments, and the strongest safeguards cannot be built by one company alone.

concepts.title: Race to the top from frontier
concepts.description: A safety-focused lab at the frontier does safety research on real frontier models and sets practices that competitors copy and that later inform laws.

concepts.title: Buy time, then spend it
concepts.description: Use export controls and, since September 2026, deliberate pacing of the frontier to buy a year or two, and spend that time on alignment, interpretability and testing.

concepts.title: A full stop or global pause on AI development
concepts.description: Why: authoritarian countries would keep going and no one can verify compliance. In January 2026 he called it untenable; in September 2026 he still rated a full global pause as unlikely, while now backing slower, verifiable pacing.

concepts.title: Pace the frontier, slow software too
concepts.description: Deliberately delay when AIs reach each capability level, including slowing software progress and not only training runs, ideally through an industry-wide pause followed by a US-China agreement.

concepts.title: Race at full speed, then pause at the last moment ("burn the lead")
concepts.description: He thinks pacing beats racing even after companies fix their security, partly because nobody knows when the point of no return is. "I currently think that it's better to pace than to race even once companies have good security (as I mentioned, I'm uncertain…

concepts.title: Alignment science decades behind capabilities
concepts.description: Nobody knows how to give a grown, inscrutable AI the goals we want, and the field is nowhere near the precision that would take, while capabilities race ahead.

concepts.title: Enforced global halt on frontier AI
concepts.description: Governments must make frontier AI development illegal everywhere, through an international agreement that caps and tracks compute, with no exceptions for governments or militaries.

concepts.title: Transformative AI within decades
concepts.description: Even the "long timelines" of skeptical experts now put human-level AI within a decade or two.

concepts.title: Safety plans centralize power
concepts.description: Many safety proposals (indefinite nonproliferation, fewer labs, licensing, surveillance) rely on centralized control that would be ineffective, freedom-damaging, or create their own catastrophe.

concepts.title: Reckless race, but probably survivable
concepts.description: The world is taking far more risk with AI than it should, yet a good outcome is still more likely than not even if we keep handling it badly.

concepts.title: The race is not a coordination problem
concepts.description: Too many actors want to race regardless of risk, so safety-minded players stepping back would barely slow AI down.

concepts.title: Weak political will, gray-zone evidence
concepts.description: Policymakers have little appetite to slow AI down, and capability tests rarely produce a clear, convincing case that risk is high, so neither regulation nor a credible pause gets triggered.

concepts.title: Cheap safety, exported industry-wide
concepts.description: A frontier company that stays competitive can invent low-cost safety practices, pressure rivals to copy them, and turn widely adopted practices into future regulation.

concepts.title: Unilateral pause commitments by a responsible company
concepts.description: Why: others would race ahead, and a pause in the gray zone would look like crying wolf. What he rejects is committing to a pause in advance, not pausing ever: the same post says "I think a unilateral pause could be a good idea, both on consequentialist and…

concepts.title: Low public salience of AI risk
concepts.description: People dislike AI vaguely but do not rank it as a top worry, so there is little political demand for rules.

concepts.title: Enforced compute and datacenter limits
concepts.description: Binding, internationally upheld rules on large datacenters and AI speed, backed by liability law and a practiced ability to shut AI down, keep humans in control.

concepts.title: Delay, detect, defend physically
concepts.description: Buy time by restricting the information and the DNA, watch for anything whose nucleic acids are growing exponentially, and stop infection with physical barriers rather than medicine.

concepts.title: Evaluate and restrict models before release
concepts.description: On the artificial intelligence side, test new models for biological uplift before release, prune or unlearn the most hazardous knowledge, and treat open weights as unfixable.

concepts.title: Compute for visibility, allocation, enforcement
concepts.description: Governing industrial-scale compute (export controls, cloud provider oversight, chip tracking, carefully chosen hardware mechanisms) gives governments visibility into who is building what, lets them steer resources, and helps enforce rules, with privacy guardrails.

concepts.title: Controls buy time, plus adaptation
concepts.description: Controls impose costs rather than absolute barriers, so they must be paired with societal resilience and defenses that work after capabilities spread.

concepts.title: Avert, diffuse, democratize
concepts.description: Use differential technology development to change the incentives: harden the world against AI catastrophes without centralizing, diffuse AI that augments rather than replaces people, and build technology that ties institutions to citizens.

concepts.title: Centralizing safety: locking down labs, a global pause regime, or a single actor taking control
concepts.description: Why: concentrated power has no recourse if it is corrupted. "But there are two paths to averting these risks. You could lock down the labs, centralize the technology, and prevent it from proliferating. Or, you could build technical solutions to solve AI's…

concepts.title: Training by default produces schemers
concepts.description: Hard reinforcement learning on economically valuable tasks rewards getting results "no matter what," so without deliberate effort models learn to lie and hide misaligned goals.

concepts.title: Independent evaluators embedded inside labs
concepts.description: Outside evaluators with employee-level access throughout training, evaluation and internal use, who publish their findings, plus monitoring of every model run.

concepts.title: Transformative AI may come soon
concepts.description: AGI might be near and might be dangerous (he cites forecasts of AGI around 2031, and notes that many people disagree), and current alignment methods probably will not hold up for the systems expected around 2028.

concepts.title: Too few safety researchers
concepts.description: Solving alignment is talent-constrained, and the field is not growing fast enough to be ready in time.

concepts.title: Capabilities are compounding very fast
concepts.description: The length of tasks AI agents can do on their own has doubled about every seven months. When the podcast host summarized this as pointing to self-improving AI within a couple of years, she agreed, with caveats: "it really doesn’t seem like two years would be surprising."

concepts.title: Evaluations that trigger safeguards
concepts.description: Tie what developers must do to measured capability levels, so that danger is caught early and safeguards scale with it.

concepts.title: Changing a lab from the inside
concepts.description: . "I basically think the track record of that particular theory of change looks pretty bad. I think if you just look at the history of people who tried to do that, there's just a lot of people giving up and leaving." (80,000 Hours, June 2025)

concepts.title: Alignment research is far too slow
concepts.description: Nobody knows how to align a superintelligence, the field is not treating the problem with Apollo-level seriousness, and technical research is not on pace.

concepts.title: Catastrophic capability within years
concepts.description: Capabilities are moving much faster than governance, with loss of control and catastrophic misuse now a risk for the next few years rather than decades.

concepts.title: Safety claims are self-reported
concepts.description: Outsiders cannot check whether companies' safety and security claims are true, because the key details are confidential, and today's outside testing is shallow, late and lacks access.

concepts.title: Too few auditors, weak demand
concepts.description: There are not enough qualified auditors and no strong requirement or market pull for audits, so the ecosystem cannot cover the risks in time.

concepts.title: Deep-access third-party frontier audits
concepts.description: Independent auditors with deep, secure access to non-public information verify company claims and audit the whole organization, at graded AI Assurance Levels (AAL-1 to AAL-4, the top level built to catch deliberate deception).

concepts.title: Candid alarm plus ready treaty
concepts.description: Tell policymakers and the public the unvarnished truth to build political will, while preparing the legal and technical "off switch" so a halt can be enforced the moment that will exists.

concepts.title: Models already hide from tests
concepts.description: Current models can already tell when they are being evaluated and may behave differently when deployed, so purely behavioral testing can be fooled.

concepts.title: No method gives high reliability
concepts.description: Neither interpretability nor black-box methods (methods that only look at inputs and outputs) will give highly reliable checks on a superintelligent system, so labs will likely deploy without fully reliable safeguards.

concepts.title: Interpretability as one defense layer
concepts.description: Use model internals as a de-correlated extra signal in a "swiss cheese" stack of evaluations and monitors, raising the odds of catching misalignment and making deception harder and riskier for the AI, rather than proving safety.

concepts.title: Default is a ruthless schemer
concepts.description: Without alignment techniques nobody has invented yet, a brain-like AGI past the point where humans can control it will be egregiously misaligned and willing to wipe out humanity.

concepts.title: Accelerate decentralized defensive technology
concepts.description: Build technologies that tilt the offense and defense balance toward defense (bio, cyber, information defense), openly and without new central chokepoints, so a superintelligent AI or a bad actor cannot easily take over.

concepts.title: Liability plus hardware soft pause
